string.text: {=krv_gt_desc_seljuk}The Great Seljuk Turks began as Oghuz steppe warriors from Central Asia before sweeping into the Islamic world, breaking the Byzantine army at Manzikert and carving out an empire stretching from Khorasan to Anatolia. Their Sultans rule through a partnership of Turkoman horse-warriors and Persian-trained viziers, blending steppe cavalry tradition with the administrative sophistication of the Nizamiyya.

{=krv_gt_desc_empire}The Byzantines are the Greek-speaking heirs of Rome in the east, ruling from Constantinople for over a thousand years. Though battered by the Seljuk conquest of Anatolia after Manzikert, they endure through disciplined thematic armies, elite guard regiments like the Varangians, and a sophisticated bureaucracy that has outlasted a dozen invading peoples before this one.

{=krv_gt_desc_aserai}The Abbasids are the Arab caliphal dynasty of Baghdad, nominal heads of the Islamic world since overthrowing the Umayyads. Though real military power now rests with Turkish ghulam guardsmen and the Great Seljuk Sultans who protect them, the Caliphs retain immense religious authority, and their court remains a center of law, scholarship, and trade linking the Mediterranean to the Indian Ocean.

{=krv_gt_desc_khuzait}The Kara-Khanids are a great Turkic steppe people, descended from Karluk and Yaghma tribes who once served the Gokturk khaganate. Since converting to Islam under Satuq Bughra Khan, they have built a settled khanate split between Samarkand and Kashgar, yet remain formidable horse archers, contesting Transoxiana and Khorasan with the Great Seljuk Sultans.

{=krv_gt_desc_sturgia}The Georgians are a Christian mountain people of the Caucasus, ruled from Tbilisi by the Bagrationi dynasty. Hemmed in by hostile neighbors on every side, they have forged a hardy warrior culture of aznauri light cavalry and eristavi noble lancers, determined to hold their highland kingdom against Seljuk raiders pressing up from the south.

{=krv_gt_desc_battania}The Armenians of Cilicia are mountain lords who broke from Byzantine rule to carve out a principality in the Taurus range. Descended from the old Armenian nobility, their azat cavalry and naxarar warlords hold their fortresses in a loose, often quarrelsome confederation, uniting readily against any outside claim on their highland refuge.

{=krv_gt_desc_vlandia}The Crusaders are Frankish and Norman lords who marched east on the First Crusade and carved out the Principality of Antioch and County of Edessa in 1098. Knights in mail and turcopole horse-archers hold their new domain on the Great Seljuk Empire's western frontier, a warrior nobility as at home besieging a fortress as riding down infidels in open battle.
